one_sentence: Correctly identifies Castelnuovo & Nisticò (2010), JEDC 34(9):1700-1731 with no field mixing, but is missing the DOI, has an accented-name inconsistency across fields (Author drops the accent, ResearcherID keeps it, ORCID drops it again), an ALL-CAPS/ampersand journal name, an unprotected "U.S." in the title, and six WoS-export artifact fields (Number="9, SI", Note, Organization, ResearcherID-Numbers, ORCID-Numbers, Unique-ID, EISSN) that should be pruned or fixed.

issues.reason: Crossref and the publisher record the second author's surname with an accent: "Nisticò" (o with grave accent). The WoS export is internally inconsistent about this: the Author field strips the accent ("Nistico"), the ResearcherID-Numbers field keeps it ("Nisticò, Salvatore/JBS-4745-2023"), and the ORCID-Numbers field strips it again ("Nistico, Salvatore/..."). The Author field is the one that renders in the bibliography and must carry the accent, written in BibTeX as Nistic\`{o} or Nistic{\`o} if not saving the file as UTF-8/using biblatex.

"SI" is Web of Science's own flag meaning "Special Issue", appended to the issue number, not part of the actual issue designation. Crossref and RePEc both give the plain issue number as 9 (this was the special issue on the 14th International Conference on Computing in Economics and Finance, but the issue number itself is simply 9).

issues.corrected: Journal of Economic Dynamics and Control
issues.reason: WoS exports journal names in all caps with an ampersand as a Library-of-Congress-style abbreviation convention; this is not the journal's actual title. The publisher (Elsevier/ScienceDirect) and Crossref both give the name in title case using "and", not "&": "Journal of Economic Dynamics and Control".

issues.original: Stock market conditions and monetary policy in a DSGE model for the U.S.
issues.corrected: Stock market conditions and monetary policy in a DSGE model for the {U.S.}
issues.reason: Title text matches the published article exactly (verified against Crossref and RePEc), so there is no field-mixing. However "U.S." is not wrapped in braces, so a non-sentence-case bibliography style (e.g. plain, unsrt) will lowercase it to "u.s." on typeset. This is a capitalization-protection hygiene fix, not a wording change.

No doi field present in the WoS export. The DOI resolves via Crossref to this exact article (title, authors, volume 34, issue 9, pages 1700-1731, year 2010 all match) and is also listed on the ScienceDirect abstract page (pii S0165188910001582).

WoS-internal ResearcherID metadata field, not a standard BibTeX field and not needed for citation; safe to drop as export cruft. (Its accented spelling of the surname was cross-checked and used to resolve the Author-field inconsistency above.)
WoS-internal ORCID metadata field, not a standard BibTeX field; author ORCID is not needed for a reference-list entry and this field duplicates/contradicts the Author field's spelling.
Web of Science's internal accession number, meaningless outside the WoS database; standard bibliography-hygiene cruft to strip.

Value itself is correct (confirmed against the ISSN portal: JEDC online ISSN is 1879-1743), but eissn is a non-standard BibTeX field for a reference-list entry; issn alone (0165-1889, also confirmed correct) suffices and is what the corrected entry keeps.

WoS conference-sponsor metadata (Society for Computational Economics, sponsor of the CEF 2008 conference referenced in Note), irrelevant to citing the journal article and not a field @article recognizes.

issues.original: 14th International Conference on Computing in Economics and Finance (CEF 2008), Univ Sorbonne, Inst Higher Learn, Paris, FRANCE, JUN 26-28, 2008
issues.reason: Multi-line WoS conference-provenance string (this JEDC special issue collected papers presented at CEF 2008); it describes the special issue's origin, not the cited article's content, and is conventional WoS-export cruft that does not belong in a citation's Note field.
